voice.purpose: Ki's message and the document body — the serif that speaks in sentences.

ui.purpose: Labels, controls, metadata — Public Sans does the interface's pointing.

typed.purpose: Margin notes, provenance, and every measurement — Courier Prime with tabular figures. Never body copy, never buttons.

shadows.name: ki-lift
shadows.purpose: A sheet resting on a ground: the delivered artifact, and the panel when the page frames it. Removed in print.

shadows.name: decision-shade
shadows.purpose: Under the sticky decision row, so the anchor reads as pinned over the scroll.

motion.name: ki-step
motion.purpose: The duration of the system's one authored moment. No other durations exist.

motion.name: ki-step-ease
motion.purpose: Paper has no easing: the mark lands in two visible steps.

motion.name: ki-land
motion.purpose: A mark lands on the page — the artifact sheet arriving. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; add no other entrances.

breakpoints.name: panel-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: The panel's margin turns under its row: the blue rule drops, a hairline takes over, notes wrap horizontally.

breakpoints.name: panel-wide
breakpoints.purpose: The framed panel narrows its inline padding to 16px.

breakpoints.name: print
breakpoints.purpose: White ground, 16mm page margin, shadows removed, panel and spec pages hidden, answer key starts a new page.

narrative.overview:
Ki's screens are pages from an exercise book. The ground is cool paper, not cream; the work is set in ink; and the margin — a faint blue rule with the review written beside the line it belongs to — is the signature move. In the panel, Ki's ink is the work and the educator's red is the marking; in the documents, the question numbers hang in the same margin. The world is quiet and document-dense: restraint is the brand posture, and the educator's work is the color. Nothing is decorative; every line on the page is either a rule the page owns or a mark someone made on it.

The system refuses the chat category's chrome and the corporate dashboard — both named by the owner as wrong. No bubbles around messages, no avatar, no card-with-accent-border, no wallpaper gradient. Chrome is deleted wherever type can carry the state: a rule, a margin note, or a label does the work. It must not read as childish or hand-drawn, and it must not read as SaaS furniture.

Two surfaces share the one world. The panel is narrow and conversation-first, designed at 440px, read beside an editor. The artifact documents — quizzes, worksheets, handouts, assignments, case studies — are restrained in the same world, printable, and the educator's to restyle. The system is plain CSS and static HTML: no JavaScript, no network, no build step; the faces are embedded locally. Light only — a dark theme is deferred, and the tokens are where it will land.
keyCharacteristics: One paper ground (#f1f2ef), ink as the only voice color, red reserved for attention.
Three type voices with strict jobs: serif message, grotesk chrome, typewriter margin.
The margin: the review sits beside the line it belongs to; question numbers hang in it.
Chrome deleted where type carries the state.
Near-square geometry (2px on controls), hairline rules as the form language.
Depth only where a sheet rests on a ground, or a decision stays pinned.
One authored motion: a mark lands in two steps. Nothing else moves.
Colour never carries meaning alone; every red mark carries words.

rules.name: The Red-Reserved Rule
rules.body: Red is the educator's, not Ki's. It is spent only on attention — a flag that needs the educator's eye — never on decoration, headings, or states of the interface. Every red mark carries its words beside it, because colour never carries meaning alone.

rules.name: The Marks-Are-Not-Ink Rule
rules.body: Body text is ink (11.5:1); labels and secondary text are secondary ink (5.2:1). Mark grey and soft red are marks and rules, never reading text — the only grey label in the system is a disabled control's.

rules.name: The No-Faux-Italic Rule
rules.body: The embedded serif has no italic face, and none is faked: em is weight 600 with a hairline underline in the panel, weight alone in documents. Never an oblique.

rules.name: The Typed-Voice Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime is the margin's voice — notes, provenance, and every measurement, aligned in columns by tabular figures. Never body copy, never buttons, never prose.

rules.name: The English-Skeleton Rule
rules.body: The document skeleton — section headings, the Q1. and 1. anchors, the Q1 — answer-key labels, the header block — is structure the repo's check script (scripts/check.py) reads. Render it exactly, in English; the content around it follows the course language.

rules.name: The Paper-Flat Rule
rules.body: Depth marks a physical sheet or an anchored decision — never a floating UI layer. No hover lifts, no card shadows, no stacked overlays.

rules.name: The Deleted-Chrome Rule
rules.body: No bubbles, no avatar, no card standing in for a label, no accent stripes; a rule, a margin note, or type itself does the work.

rules.name: The Margin Rule
rules.body: The margin carries the review — ticks, provenance, the red mark, question numbers — beside the line each belongs to. It is never a sidebar and never a second column of content.

rules.name: The One-Moment Rule
rules.body: The system has one authored motion: a mark lands in two steps — a clip-path wipe, 140ms, steps(2, end), disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Paper has no easing; add no entrances, no easing curves, no hover motion to sections.

dos: Do spend red only on attention, and only with its words beside the mark (#b8372e, 5.2:1 on paper).
Do set all voice text in ink (#20324f) and labels and secondary text in secondary ink (#55657e).
Do put the review in the margin, beside the row it belongs to (6.5rem column in the panel; hanging numbers in documents).
Do keep the typed voice to margin notes and measurements, with tabular figures (.ki-num) for counts, points, and minutes.
Do keep answer areas as empty ruled lines and keep questions whole across page and print breaks.
Do render the English skeleton exactly (Q1., Q1 —, the header block) — scripts/check.py reads it.
Do check every document in print emulation before delivery (white ground, 16mm margin, shadows off).
donts: Don't add chat chrome: no bubbles, no avatar, no card-with-accent-border, no wallpaper gradient.
Don't set reading text in mark grey (#9aa09b) or soft red (#dfb3ae) — they are marks and rules.
Don't use red for decoration, headings, or states of the interface.
Don't fake an italic — the serif has none; emphasis is weight 600.
Don't add a hosted font, a CDN, a build step, or JavaScript; marks are inline SVG, never a unicode glyph or an emoji.
Don't add motion beyond the one mark-landing moment.
Don't turn the margin into a sidebar or a second column of content.
